testDemos.title: Long Tick Label Pruning
testDemos.description: A date axis with long formatted tick labels, pruned as space runs out instead of overlapping.
testDemos.notes: The group axis is type date on an ordinal scale with tickLabelFormat "%B %e, %Y", so each of the 26 daily group values wants a label as long as "March 18, 2016" over a single area series. Date axes leave tickLabelTruncationEnabled at its false default, so rather than shortening the text the axis fits a tick count to the available width and then shows only every nth label, also hiding any label that would overhang the plot edge and always keeping one. Narrowing the chart drops the surviving labels in steps instead of letting them collide.

testDemos.title: Threshold Group Line
testDemos.description: A titled threshold line at a fixed date on the group axis, over a linear date scale.
testDemos.notes: groupAxisConfig sets threshold to a timestamp on March 12 2017 plus a thresholdTitle, thresholdTitlePadding of 5px all round and thresholdTitleBefore false, which places the title on the later side of the line. The scale is linear rather than ordinal, so the quarter-hour samples sit at their real spacing along the axis. The data is a daylight-saving transition: the raw date values change offset from -04:00 to -03:00 partway through, so the wall-clock times repeat, while displayProperty ("display") supplies the plain climbing 01:00 to 03:45 labels used on the axis and in the tooltip.

testDemos.title: Group Ordinal
testDemos.description: String group values placed in even slots by an ordinal group scale.
testDemos.notes: The group axis is type string with scale ordinal, so the 26 three-letter groups (AAA through ZZZ) each get an equal slot in data order, with a line series over value1 and an area series over value2 sharing one series axis. Because the type is string, tickLabelTruncationEnabled defaults to true, so crowded labels are shortened with an ellipsis instead of being skipped the way the date axes in the other tick demos are.

testDemos.title: Ordinal Dates
testDemos.description: Date group values kept on an ordinal scale, with month-formatted tick labels.
testDemos.notes: The group axis is type date but scale ordinal, so every month gets the same slot width regardless of how many days it has, and tickLabelFormat "%B %Y" (matched by valueFormat for the tooltip) spells the months out in full. tickLabelTruncationEnabled is explicitly false, so those wide labels are dropped rather than shortened, and the series axis fixes min at 0 with a currency tickLabelFormat of "$.0f". The data is 25 consecutive months in which many have no total at all, so the single stacked bar series leaves visible gaps.

testDemos.title: Group Display Property
testDemos.description: A displayProperty on the group axis: groups keyed by one property but labeled by another.
testDemos.notes: The axis keys on "group" (the integers 1 to 28) while displayProperty points at "groupDisplay", so tick labels and tooltips show the two-letter names, which cycle aa to ee and therefore repeat even though the underlying keys are all distinct. The scale is ordinal, so the 28 rows sit in data order at even slots, with a bar series (value1) and a line series (value2) on one series axis.

testDemos.title: Monthly
testDemos.description: A year of monthly data on an ordinal date axis with rotated, abbreviated month tick labels.
testDemos.notes: The group axis is a UTC date axis on an ordinal scale with tickCount 12, tick labels formatted '%b' and rotated 45 degrees, while the tooltip spells the month out in full (valueFormat '%B', valueLabel 'Group'). Both bar series share one stack (SS0) on a single series axis pinned to min 0 with SI currency ticks ('$s'), and markerShape null keeps the segments plain. The bundled data is the twelve months of 2015 with amounts in the tens to hundreds of thousands; its value3 column is unused by the config, so it only shows up under the data tab's Unused toggle. Animation durations sit at 300ms across the board, with a 500ms focus.

testDemos.title: Capped
testDemos.description: Bar series comparing round, curve and point caps, with and without cap expansion.
testDemos.notes: Seven bar series draw four value columns with capType 'round', 'curve', 'point' and null at capSize 15, each shape appearing twice — once with capExpand false and once true — so you can see what happens when a cap is larger than the bar it sits on. The series axis is pinned to min -5000 and max 5000 while the bundled data is only plus or minus 100 and plus or minus 1000 across ten weekly dates, with several columns omitted per row, which keeps most bars shorter than their caps and leaves visible gaps. Group ticks are rotated 45 degrees with tickCount 12 on an ordinal UTC date axis, and the animation durations are deliberately slow — 8s initial and value-change, 1.5s expansion and collapse, 800ms focus — so the caps can be watched stretching and shrinking.

testDemos.title: Capped Inverted
testDemos.description: The capped bars demo with the plot inverted so the bars run horizontally.
testDemos.notes: plotConfig.inverted true is the substantive change: the group axis runs top-to-bottom and the seven capped bar series grow sideways, so the caps are drawn on the left and right ends rather than the top and bottom. The group axis also gains a tick label format ('%b') and a full-month tooltip format ('%B') and is retitled 'Month' instead of 'Date', all of which the upright version leaves off. Series order is regrouped as well — Round, Curve and Point first, then the three Expand variants — so the legend and the grouped bar slots pair the cap types differently; capSize 15, the -5000 to 5000 series axis, the slow 8s value-change animation and the same cap-data.json are all shared with the upright demo.

testDemos.title: Daylight Savings
testDemos.description: Quarter-hourly groups spanning a daylight-savings transition, labeled through a display property.
testDemos.notes: The data is sixteen quarter-hour samples around a clock change: eight at UTC-04:00 running 01:00 to 02:45, then eight at UTC-03:00 starting again at 02:00, so the 02:00-02:45 wall-clock block appears twice and the second block actually resolves to earlier UTC instants. The ordinal group axis keeps the rows in file order rather than sorting by instant, and its displayProperty points at a separate 'display' column carrying the same wall-clock times, so ticks and tooltips read as local time instead of the raw offset dates. A single line series with 1s initial, expansion, value-change and collapse durations keeps the transition easy to follow.

testDemos.title: Cluttered
testDemos.description: Nine series across two axes — lines, bars, grouped bars and stacked areas — crowded onto one plot.
testDemos.notes: Axis SA0 carries a marker line, a black-filled bar with a light stroke and an area, while SA1 carries another line, two bars grouped through seriesGroupConfigs (SG0) and three areas stacked through seriesStackConfigs (SS1), all at markerSize 6. Both series axes take axisLineMargin 3 from seriesAxisAllConfig and sit on opposite sides (SA0 before, SA1 after), and the tooltip is restyled to padding 1 with a translucent grey background and a 3px black border so the overlapping hit targets are easy to see. The bundled data is 26 rows of small values (0-35) on a numeric ordinal group axis whose groupNO column is deliberately out of order for the first six rows.

testDemos.title: Cluttered Inverted
testDemos.description: The cluttered demo with the plot inverted so every series runs horizontally.
testDemos.notes: plotConfig.inverted true and the title are the only differences from the cluttered config, so the group axis runs top-to-bottom, all nine series grow left to right, and the two series axes end up above and below the plot instead of to its left and right. Inverting also changes what crowds: the 26 numeric group labels stack down the side one per row rather than colliding horizontally, while the grouped bars and three-deep area stack compete for horizontal space. Everything else is shared — axisLineMargin 3, the restyled tooltip, markerSize 6, the 1s animation durations and the same mixed-groups-positive-values-data.json.

testDemos.title: Missing Values
testDemos.description: Six line, area and bar series over a holey dataset, all taking the default break at the gap.
testDemos.notes: No series sets skipMissing or showMissingAtBase, so every hole gets the default treatment: lines and areas break at the missing group while bars just leave their slot empty. The six properties go missing in different groups, so the treatments rarely line up — value0 to value2 (line, bar, area) sit on Series Axis 1, value3 on Series Axis 2, and value4/value5 share seriesGroupConfigs slot SG0 as side-by-side bars — and three rows (groups 1, 31 and 38) carry no values at all, leaving empty slots on the ordinal group axis. The tooltip still lists the absent series rather than hiding them, via tooltipConfig.showMissingValues with missingValueText "N/A".

testDemos.title: Missing Stacked Values
testDemos.description: Three area series in one stack, each with holes in different groups.
testDemos.notes: value6, value7 and value8 all come through seriesAllConfig as areas on the single stack SS1 (seriesStackConfigs), on an axis whose softMin/softMax of 0 keeps the base in the domain. A missing value contributes nothing to the running total, so that series breaks at the gap — the default treatment, with neither skipMissing nor showMissingAtBase set — and the series above it close down onto the ones below for that group. Each property is missing in its own set of groups so the stack rarely loses two layers at once, except in the three rows with no values at all (groups 1, 31 and 38) where the whole stack disappears, and the tooltip reports the absent layers as "N/A" (showMissingValues, missingValueText).

testDemos.title: Missing Ranged Values
testDemos.description: Two ranged series where one end of a span, or both, can be missing.
testDemos.notes: The ranged area spans value1 to value0 and the ranged bar value3 to value2 (property plus rangeProperty), and skipPartialRange is left at false, so a group with only one of the two ends defined does not count as missing — it collapses to a zero-extent span at the value that is there, and the area stays connected through it as a flat pinch. Only where both ends are absent does the default break apply, which here means the three rows that carry no values at all (groups 1, 31 and 38). The tooltip prints both ends joined by rangeValueText, so a half-missing group reads as a value next to "N/A" (showMissingValues, missingValueText).

testDemos.title: Missing Single Values
testDemos.description: One group with one defined value, and eight other series with nothing to draw.
testDemos.notes: The data is a single row (group 1, value0 = 3) against nine configured series, so one line on Series Axis 1 draws a lone marker while everything else — the bar and area on the same axis, the line on Series Axis 2, the two bars sharing seriesGroupConfigs slot SG0, and the three-area stack SS1 — is entirely missing. With the default treatment (no skipMissing, no showMissingAtBase) there is nothing to break or bridge; what the demo exercises is the degenerate case, where the axes, the single ordinal group slot and the legend all have to lay out from the config rather than from the data. Every empty series still gets a tooltip row of "N/A" (showMissingValues, missingValueText) beside the one real value.

testDemos.title: Skip Missing Values
testDemos.description: Missing values skipped: shapes connect across the gaps instead of breaking.
testDemos.notes: The same six series as the Missing Values demo — line, bar and area on Series Axis 1, a line plus a grouped bar pair on Series Axis 2 — with skipMissing turned on for all of them through seriesAllConfig. Each property drops out at a different group (Value 0 at group 3, Value 1 at 4, Value 2 at 5 and so on, with longer runs further along), and groups 1, 31 and 38 carry no values at all, so the lines and areas now run straight from the last defined group to the next and draw no marker at the groups they jump. The bars have nothing to join across, so they look exactly as they do without skipping, and the tooltip still lists every absent series as N/A (tooltipConfig.showMissingValues with missingValueText).

testDemos.title: Skip Missing Stacked Values
testDemos.description: Three stacked areas skipping their missing values, so each band closes across its own gaps.
testDemos.notes: The three areas share one stack (seriesStackConfigs plus a seriesAllConfig that sets renderer, stack and skipMissing) on a single axis with base 0 and softMin/softMax of 0. Skipping is per band rather than per group: Value 6 is missing at groups 9, 16, 17 and 36, Value 7 at 9, 10, 14, 15, 36 and 37, and Value 8 at 11 and 12, so a band draws straight from its last defined group to its next while the remaining bands still stack over the reduced total at the group in between — which is why the bands can overlap there instead of sitting cleanly on one another. Groups 1, 31 and 38 have no values at all and drop out of all three bands, and the tooltip still reports each absent band as N/A.

testDemos.title: Skip Missing Ranged Values
testDemos.description: Ranged (min/max) series that skip only the groups where both ends are missing.
testDemos.notes: A ranged area spanning value0 to value1 and a ranged bar spanning value2 to value3, each setting skipMissing on the series itself. skipPartialRange is left off, so a group with just one of the two properties defined still counts as present and collapses to a zero-extent span at the value it does have — only groups missing both ends are actually skipped, which is groups 1, 26, 31, 32 and 38 for the area and just the three wholly empty groups 1, 31 and 38 for the bar. The half-missing groups (value0 at 3, value1 at 4, value2 at 5, value3 at 6, plus the later runs) therefore read as pinch points: the area stays connected straight through them and the ranged bar flattens away to nothing.

testDemos.title: Skip Missing Single Values
testDemos.description: One data group with only one of nine series defined, every series skipping its missing values.
testDemos.notes: The dataset is a single row — group 1 with a value0 of 3 — against nine series spread over two axes, a grouped bar pair and a three-area stack, all carrying skipMissing from seriesAllConfig. The eight series with no value draw nothing at all, and Value 0 has just the one point so its line has no segment to draw either, leaving a lone circle marker; all nine still appear in the legend and the tooltip reports the missing eight as N/A. This is the degenerate end of the skip path, where an empty shape and a one-point shape both have to survive layout and animation.

testDemos.title: Missing All Values
testDemos.description: Every group empty — a stack and a bar group configured over data with no values at all.
testDemos.notes: The dataset is seven rows carrying nothing but their group value, so none of the six series has a value to draw: value0 to value2 are stacked on SS0 against Series Axis 1, and value3 plus the SG0 bar pair sit on Series Axis 2. Nothing sets skipMissing or showMissingAtBase, so this is the default missing treatment taken to its limit — an all-gap chart that has to lay out seven ordinal group slots, empty series axes, an empty stack and empty grouped-bar slots, with every tooltip row reading "N/A" (showMissingValues, missingValueText).

demos.title: Stacked
demos.description: Two stacks — bars on one value axis, areas on another.
demos.notes: Each stack is a seriesStackConfigs entry pinned to its own axis (SS0 on the left, SS1 on the right), and every series simply names its stack and axis. Both axes set base 0 with softMin/softMax 0, so the zero baseline stays in view even when the data sits entirely above it, and stacked series animate as one gapless unit through every transition.

demos.title: Grouped
demos.description: Four bar series clustered side by side in each group slot, drawn over a fifth ungrouped series that keeps the full slot.
demos.notes: One seriesGroupConfigs entry collects the clustered series: the group slot is split evenly between its members, with groupAxisConfig.groupPadding.inner as the gap. The first series opts out with group: null, so it keeps the full slot width and renders behind the cluster — the usual backdrop or total pattern. The value axis pins min to 0, so every bar in the slot measures from a common zero.

demos.title: Grouped Across Axes
demos.description: Two bar series grouped side by side while each scales against its own value axis.
demos.notes: Both series share the sole seriesGroupConfigs entry so they cluster in each slot, but one names axis SA0 (drawn before the plot) and the other SA1 (after), each pinned to min 0. The sample data deliberately pairs a single-digit property (value1) with one in the hundreds (value8) over string groups on an ordinal scale, so the bars are only comparable because each reads its own scale.

demos.title: Stacked & Grouped
demos.description: Stacking and grouping composed: four series in two stacks, placed side by side within each group.
demos.notes: Every series names both a stack (SS0/SS1) and a group (SG0/SG1): the group id decides which sub-slot of the group slot the bar occupies, the stack id decides what it accumulates on. Each group slot therefore holds two side-by-side columns, each a two-segment stack, all sharing one value axis with min 0.

demos.title: Color and Base Property
demos.description: A bar series colored from a data property (colorProperty), split into two ramps either side of a colorBase.
demos.notes: colorProperty points at the same property the bars plot, so the fill tracks the bar itself, and colorBase 0 cuts the ramp in two: colorBaseBelowMin/colorBaseBelowMax run saturated red at the most negative value up to pale red at the base, colorBaseAboveMin/colorBaseAboveMax run pale to saturated blue above it, both interpolated in HCL (colorInterpolation). Each half fits its own end of the color property's extent, so the deepest red and deepest blue are always the current extremes. The series axis pins base 0 so the bars grow out of the same divide the colors are split on.

demos.title: Color Property
demos.description: Bars colored per data row from a color property in the data instead of the series config.
demos.notes: One bar series reads both its height and its fill from the same property, interpolating in HCL from colorMin (#8f8fff) to colorMax (#0000ff) across the color property's extent — the palest bar is always the smallest value and the darkest the largest, however the numbers move. Setting colorProperty is what switches a series off its single palette color; leaving it null gives the usual per-series color. Compare the Color and Base Property demo, which splits the same ramp in two around a colorBase.

demos.title: Axis Suppression Adjustment
demos.description: Stacked bars and two lines on separate value axes, whose domains rescale as the legend suppresses series.
demos.notes: seriesAxisAllConfig.adjustForSuppression is on for both axes, so hiding a series from the legend recomputes that axis' domain instead of leaving dead space behind. The three bars fall into the sole seriesStackConfigs entry (pinned to SA0) while the two lines opt out with stack: null and read SA1 on the other side, so each axis rescales independently. All four animation durations are stretched to 2000ms to make the rescale easy to follow.

demos.title: Multiple Axes
demos.description: Eight line series over a linear date axis, spread across four separate value axes.
demos.notes: Four seriesAxisConfigs entries sit two before the plot and two after (before), pairing each raw series with its running total on its own scale — the two currency axes format ticks as $s, and the count pair sits on the right. Grid lines are off in seriesAxisAllConfig and re-enabled on SA2 only, so four axes' worth of lines do not pile up, and seriesAllConfig.markerShape null leaves bare lines. The data is one UTC day of sales sampled every few minutes (182 rows) on a linear date group axis labelled %_H:%M, where per-sample sales peak near 8k against a running total near 78k — hence the split axes.

demos.title: Threshold Line
demos.description: Two series axes, each drawing its own threshold line and title across the plot.
demos.notes: The left axis carries three stacked bars with threshold 20; the right axis carries two unstacked lines with threshold -5, and because the bars and the lines read different scales the two threshold lines sit at unrelated heights. thresholdTitle labels both, with thresholdTitleBefore putting one label on the low side and the other on the high side and thresholdTitleSnapToValue flipping a label that has no room left. The axes also differ in adjustForSuppression: hiding a stacked series from the legend rescales the left axis and its threshold line rides along, while the right axis keeps its domain. All four animation durations are stretched to 2000ms, so the rescaling is easy to follow.

demos.title: Truncated Text
demos.description: Over-long title, axis, legend and tick label text fitted by the truncation settings.
demos.notes: The chart title is deliberately too long and carries a titlePrefix and titleSuffix in their own boxes, with truncationEnabled/truncationValue trimming it to "..." instead of overflowing; both axis titles do the same through titleTruncationEnabled. The group axis truncates tick labels to their slot (tickLabelTruncationEnabled) rather than dropping ticks, with tickLabelTruncationMaxPercent capping how much of the chart a label may occupy when it runs perpendicular to the axis. Labels come from displayProperty ("groupDisplay", phrases up to "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious is long") while the numeric group property still drives positioning, and every box in the chart is stroked grey so the bounds the text is being fitted into are visible.

demos.title: Positive Negative Labels
demos.description: An inverted (horizontal) bar chart with labelProperty value labels inside bars running either side of zero.
demos.notes: plotConfig.inverted turns the group axis vertical, so the single bar series grows left and right from a zero base (seriesAxisConfigs base 0, with softMin/softMax 0 holding zero in view even when the values sit on one side). labelProperty reads the same value7 column the bars are drawn from and draws it white inside the value end of each bar (labelPosition 'inside', labelOffset -2), while labelMinPositionPercent and labelMinRangePercent — both 0.05 — drop the label from any bar too short to hold it. The bundled data pairs string group names with small mixed-sign values, so several bars fall under that threshold.

demos.title: Stacked Labels
demos.description: Stacked areas over a linear numeric group axis with value labels on every segment.
demos.notes: An empty seriesStackConfigs entry declares a single stack, so all three area series join it and animate as one unit, and each series points labelProperty at its own value property so every segment is labelled rather than just the total. Labels sit at the outer edge of each band (seriesAllConfig labelPosition 'outside') and labelMinRangePercent 0.05 hides them on segments spanning less than a twentieth of the axis. The group axis is numeric with a linear scale (groupNL), so the groups sit at their real numeric positions and the spacing between stacks is uneven.

demos.title: Christmas Tree Bars
demos.description: A holiday novelty: one bar series where every bar takes a different palette color.
demos.notes: fillColor and strokeColor are set to "groupIndex" rather than the default "seriesIndex", so each bar picks up the colorPaletteConfig entry for its position on the group axis instead of the one color of its series — 26 groups against a 20-color palette, so the sequence wraps around near the end. The series axis pins min 0 so the strung-out colors all sit on a common baseline.

demos.title: Positive Negative Currency
demos.description: Area and line series mixing positive and negative currency values over a date axis, one series per value axis.
demos.notes: Two series axes are declared — SA0 before (left) for the small-dollar line and SA1 after (right) for the large-dollar area — while seriesAxisAllConfig gives both a zero base and a '$.2f' tick label format. The date group axis uses an ordinal scale, so dates occupy evenly spaced slots instead of a continuous timeline. Both bundled columns cross zero, so the area fills above and below its base and each axis has to cover both directions.

demos.title: Rotated Ticks
demos.description: A dense date group axis with tick labels rotated 90 degrees, and series axis labels at 45.
demos.notes: tickLabelRotation is 90 on the group axis and 45 on the series axis, which keeps 26 date labels and a set of wide three-digit value labels from colliding. The dates are rendered by tickLabelFormat ("%Y-%m-%d") and the ordinal scale gives every date an equal slot regardless of the real gaps between them.

demos.title: Range
demos.description: A low/high band drawn from rangeProperty behind a line with markers.
demos.notes: The band series reads range-max as its property and range-min as its rangeProperty, so the area spans between the two values instead of growing from the axis base, and turns markers off with markerShape null. The overlaid Middle line rides inside the band with star markers at markerSize 8. Group values are plain integers on an ordinal number axis.

demos.title: Positive Negative Range
demos.description: Range areas and floating bars whose two ends straddle zero, via rangeProperty.
demos.notes: Three series pair value1/value2, value3/value4 and value5/value6 through rangeProperty — two areas and one bar renderer — so every shape floats between its two ends rather than starting at the axis. The series axis sets base 0, which separates the positive and negative directions and gives entering and leaving shapes their resting position; seriesAllConfig turns markers off for all three (markerShape null).

demos.title: Bubble Chart
demos.description: A bubble chart: renderer 'none' with markers sized per value through markerProperty.
demos.notes: Both series set renderer 'none' in seriesAllConfig, so only the markers are drawn, and each takes its radius from a separate data column (markerProperty marker1 and marker2) interpolated between minMarkerSize 3 and markerSize 24 — the second series uses cross markers to show that the scaling is not circle-only. Every animation duration is raised to 1000ms so growth and shrink are easy to follow.

demos.title: Scatter
demos.description: A scatter chart: marker-only series (renderer none) on a linear group axis.
demos.notes: Points are positioned by irregular measured x values rather than evenly spaced groups: the group axis is a number property on scale 'linear', so the gaps in the data (0.4, 1.1, 1.5, 2.8, ...) are preserved as real distances. All three series share renderer 'none' and markerSize 6 from seriesAllConfig and are told apart by markerShape alone — star, cross and wye.

demos.title: Picket Fence Bars
demos.description: Stacked bars whose segments carry round, curve and point caps, over rotated month tick labels.
demos.notes: An empty seriesStackConfigs entry puts all three bar series in one stack, and each sets its own capType — 'round', 'curve' and 'point' — at capSize 15, so every segment ends in a different shape (markerShape null keeps the bars otherwise plain). The month axis formats ticks as '%b' rotated 45 degrees with tickCount 12 and shows full month names in the tooltip (valueFormat '%B'), while the value axis pins min to 0 and uses an SI currency tick format ('$s'). The bundled data is the twelve months of 2015 with amounts in the tens to hundreds of thousands. Animation is deliberately slow — 3s initial and value-change against 1.5s expansion and collapse — so the caps can be watched stretching and sliding as the values change.

demos.title: Pos/Neg Picket Fence Bars
demos.description: Capped bars crossing zero, with a small-dollar and a large-dollar series on their own value axes.
demos.notes: Both bar series carry caps at capSize 15 — capType 'point' on the small-dollar series, 'curve' on the large one — drawn at the value end of each bar, so they point downward on negative values. The series sit on separate axes (SA0 before, SA1 after) because their magnitudes differ by two orders of magnitude in the bundled data; seriesAxisAllConfig gives both base 0, softMin/softMax 0 and '$.2f' tick labels so each keeps zero on screen. The group axis is ordinal over dates, so bars keep equal slots regardless of date gaps. The animation durations are lopsided — 3s for a value change against 300ms enter and exit — so bars sweep through the base slowly while the caps track their moving ends.

demos.title: Curved Lines
demos.description: Line and area series drawn with different d3 curve types over a linear date axis.
demos.notes: Each dataset is drawn twice: Sales A as a natural-curve area under a plain linear line, and Sales B as a step area under its own linear line (curve types 'natural' and 'step'), so the smoothing is visible against the raw path. The group axis is a UTC date axis on a linear scale with a %_H:%M tick format, and the data is roughly 130 irregularly spaced minute-level readings, so the points are spaced by elapsed time rather than by index. The series axis pins min to 0, holding both areas above a common baseline, and every animation runs at 500ms.

demos.title: Gradients
demos.description: Areas and bars filled with linear and radial gradients referenced by id.
demos.notes: Four gradients are defined once and referenced by id from each series' gradient property: LG0 and LG1 are linear (linearGradientAllConfig makes both run top to bottom, LG1 adding rotation 45), RG0 and RG1 are radial off a shared cx/cy/r of 0.5, with RG1 shifting its focal point to fx/fy 0.75. All four are two-stop ramps at 0.8 opacity — red to blue, or blue to green — and they are split across two area and two bar series so the same fills show against both shape types (markerShape null keeps the areas unmarked). The bundled data is small positive values over an ordinal numeric group axis. All four animation durations are 500ms with a 700ms focus, so the gradient fills stay smooth as the shapes resize.

demos.title: Missing Values
demos.description: Three series over the same gaps, showing the default break next to skipMissing and showMissingAtBase.
demos.notes: Several groups carry no values at all, so all three series hit identical holes: the first breaks its line at the gap, "Base Missing" (showMissingAtBase) drops the missing points onto the series axis base of 0, and "Skip Missing" (skipMissing) joins straight across to the next defined value. Distinct markerShapes (circle, square, triangle) keep the three treatments apart where the lines cross. The tooltip still lists the absent series rather than hiding them, via tooltipConfig.showMissingValues with missingValueText "N/A".

demos.title: Missing Pos/Neg Stacked Values
demos.description: A bar stack with missing positive and negative values — segments stay coherent while the stack animates.
demos.notes: All three series share one stack (seriesStackConfigs plus seriesAllConfig), so positives pile up from the base while negatives pile down and a group's stack can straddle 0; softMin/softMax of 0 keep the base in the domain whichever way the data leans. A missing value contributes nothing to the running total, so its segment simply drops out and the segments after it close down onto the ones below — and a few groups have no values at all, leaving an empty slot. Each series sets capType "round" with capOnlyStackOuter, so the rounded cap only draws on whichever segment ends up on the outside of the stack, and the tooltip reports missing series as "N/A" (showMissingValues, missingValueText).

demos.title: Histogram
demos.description: Raw samples binned into touching bars by the createHistogram helper.
demos.notes: The helper bins the sample array — here at a fixed binWidth of 25, in place of the default nice-rounded binCount — and hands back the data rows plus the groupAxisConfig and seriesConfig fragments the demo's config is built from; the ordinal group axis with groupPadding inner and outer of 0 is what makes the bars touch. Each row carries binStart, binEnd, binCenter and count alongside the charted value, so the bin edges are available for labels and tooltips (binLabel formats each bin's tick text from its edges, and normalize can swap raw counts for probability or density).

demos.title: Waterfall
demos.description: Floating increase/decrease bars accumulating into totals, built by the createWaterfall helper.
demos.notes: createWaterfall turns a list of labelled deltas and total markers into rows holding a shared "start" range property plus the step's end under the property matching its direction, and returns three bar series — increase, decrease and total — in its default CVD-safe aqua/red/blue. Because only one of the three properties is defined per step, every series sets skipMissing with skipPartialRange so the other two draw nothing there, and group and stack are null so all three share the same slot; the two total steps span from the base (createWaterfall's base option, worth mirroring on the series axis) instead of floating. The bundled data is a nine-step fictional income statement.

demos.title: Heatmap
demos.description: A weekday-by-month grid from the createHeatmap helper.
demos.notes: Row bands sit on a tick-labelled axis, with cells colored from a shared sequential ramp. createHeatmap is handed nothing but the twelve column labels, so the ramp keeps its defaults — colorMin #cde2fb to colorMax #0d366b interpolated in lab space — and every cell keeps the default cellPadding of 0.03 trimmed off each side, which the group axis picks up as groupPadding inner 0.06 and outer 0.03. Each weekday is a bar series floating on its own one-unit band via rangeProperty, with colorProperty and tooltipProperty both pointing at the cell value and showInLegend false, and the sole series axis is pinned to min 0 / max 7 with zero margins plus one explicit ticks entry per row at its band center. The bundled grid is a seasonal curve that peaks in January and bottoms out in July on every row, and Saturday's April cell is deliberately empty, so skipMissing leaves a hole in the grid rather than a zero-height cell.

demos.title: Candlestick
demos.description: OHLC candles from the createCandlestick helper: direction-colored bodies over thin wicks.
demos.notes: The bodies span open/close and the wicks low/high, on an ordinal axis that skips non-trading days, with the volume option's pane of direction-colored volume bars along the bottom. volume: true is the only option passed, so the wicks keep the default wickWidthPercent of 0.15 under full-slot bodies (bodyWidthPercent 1) and the pane keeps its default 20% height and 5% gap — expressed purely as domain margins, with the price axis reserving the lower band through minMarginPercent 0.33 and the hidden volume axis (visible false) taking min 0 with maxMarginPercent 4. Each of the six series is defined for one direction only, so skipMissing with skipPartialRange drops the other, and the wick and volume series stay out of the legend (showInLegend false) while followSeries makes them filter and focus with their body; valueLabel titles their tooltip rows Range and Volume. The bundled walk is twenty June trading days between about $85 and $102, ten up and ten down, with volumes from roughly 414k to 1.3M — the days that moved most traded most.

demos.title: Hollow Candlestick
demos.description: The candlestick's hollow variant (createCandlestick with hollow: true).
demos.notes: Up bodies are outlined and down bodies filled, and wicks are split into segments so nothing shows through the hollow interior. hollow: true is the only option passed, so the bodies still take the full slot and the wicks the default 0.15 of it, and the up body goes to fillOpacity 0 with focusedFillOpacity and defocusedFillOpacity pinned there too, plus strokeWidth 2 thickening to focusedStrokeWidth 3 — hovering an up candle thickens its outline instead of filling it. The original low/high wick series drops to renderer 'none' (markerShape null, with a labelFillColor for its tooltip chip) and survives only as the single Range row, while four segment series above and below the bodies do the actual drawing with showInTooltip false. That split is also why the rows carry an extra upOpen column: an up candle's lower segment spans low to open, and the shared open column is defined on every row, so it cannot gate the segment by direction on its own.

demos.title: OHLC Bars
demos.description: OHLC tick bars from the createOhlc helper: a thin low/high line per trading day.
demos.notes: Each bar carries a left open tick and a right close tick, direction-colored, on an ordinal axis that skips non-trading days. createOhlc is called with no options at all, so the vertical low/high line takes the default lineWidthPercent of 0.15 and each tick the default tickWidthPercent of 0.5, reaching from the slot edge in to the center line. The ticks are zero-extent range bars — property and rangeProperty read the same open or close value — that barMinExtent inflates into 2px marks, with barAlignPercent 0 pinning the open tick to the left half of the slot and 1 the close tick to the right; the lines carry the legend entries while the ticks sit out of it (showInLegend false) and followSeries their line, so filtering or focusing a direction moves the whole bar. Twenty June trading days are bundled, without the volume column the candlestick demo has, and each bar's tooltip lists Range, Open and Close (valueLabel), the equal-ended tick ranges collapsing to single values.

demos.title: Error Bars
demos.description: Native error bars from the errorLowProperty/errorHighProperty series config.
demos.notes: Two grouped bar series and a line series each carry absolute confidence bounds, drawn as capped whiskers centered on every bar sub-slot and line point. errorLowProperty and errorHighProperty name absolute values in series axis units rather than deltas from the plotted value, and the bounds join the axis domain, so a whisker is never clipped by the top of the plot. Plant A and Plant B share the sole seriesGroupConfigs entry (plants) so their whiskers track their sub-slots, while the Target line opts out with group: null; no whisker styling is set, so the defaults apply — errorBarCapSize 6 clamped to the bar slot, errorBarStrokeWidth 1.5 and errorBarStrokeOpacity 0.9 rising to 1 on the focused series. The twelve bundled months follow a seasonal curve with deliberately asymmetric margins above and below each value, and the Target line's interval is far tighter than either plant's.

demos.title: Pie
demos.description: A pie chart from the createPie helper and chartConfig.type 'pie'.
demos.notes: Every slice is its own series, so the legend lists the slices, hovering one focuses it and clicking suppresses it (the remaining slices grow to fill the circle). Click the chart for a tooltip with one row per slice, each showing the value and its share (pieConfig.tooltipValues 'valuePercent').

demos.title: Donut
demos.description: The pie chart with an inner radius (pieConfig.innerRadiusPercent) and percent labels.
demos.notes: The labels sit at the slice centroids (pieConfig.showLabels); labels on slices thinner than labelMinAnglePercent hide themselves. The tooltip shows each slice's share too (pieConfig.tooltipValues 'percent'), and both renormalize against the remaining slices as you suppress one.

demos.title: Gauge
demos.description: A half-donut gauge via pieConfig.startAngle/endAngle (-90 to 90).
demos.notes: Three sentiment segments with rounded, padded slices, title labels at the centroids, and a live center total (pieConfig.showCenterTotal) that counts along with value changes and suppression. Its tooltip pairs each segment's share with its response count (pieConfig.tooltipValues 'percentValue'). Hovering a legend entry explodes nothing here — compare the donut demo's focusOffsetPercent.
